title: Modulation of imine rotation in photoexcited anthracene Schiff bases: role of solvent and temperature
content: Anthracene substituted imines can undergo intramolecular charge transfer (CT) and excited-state rotation around the imine bond, producing conformations that determine their photophysical properties. In the present study, we synthesised and investigated two structurally related anthracene-based Schiff bases, benzylidene-2-anthrylamine (2AAB) and o-methoxybenzylidene-2-anthrylamine (2AOMB), to understand their excited-state photophysical behaviour. Both molecules exhibited similar emission profiles, with an increase in emission intensity at longer wavelengths as solvent polarity increased from toluene to acetonitrile. Time-correlated single-photon counting analysis showed a biexponential decay, with the long lived component twice as significant as the shorter lived one. This indicates that a CT like contribution likely accounts for the long-lived component. At low temperature (100 K), the emission was enhanced, whereas it decreased as the temperature increased. 2AAB showed a sixfold increase at 100 K as compared to room temperature, while 2AOMB showed only a twofold difference. The theoretical calculations indicate that twisting of the imine bond towards an S1/S0 conical intersection provides a nonradiative relaxation pathway in both compounds. This mechanism helps explain the experimentally observed fluorescence differences by linking imine twisting to solvent friction and local solvation, which shift the balance between radiative and nonradiative decay pathways. In 2AOMB, the ortho-methoxy substituent may alter the molecule's interactions with its surrounding environment, further shifting the balance between radiative and nonradiative decay pathways.
